confidence.rationale: DataPackage.ResourceMap is separate from AvailableFormats and Properties, and the changed transfer helper never copies it.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve resource-map entries during package transfer
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve resource-map entries during package transfer

**Severity:** `high`

`DataPackageTransfer.Copy` reconstructs the package from properties and available formats, but it never reads or copies `DataPackageView.GetResourceMapAsync()` entries. Resource-backed formats can therefore lose their referenced streams when the package is forwarded through the shelf. Prepare the source resource map while the package is available and copy those entries into the destination before registering deferred format providers.

confidence.rationale: The current AllowedOperations expression adds Move to data-backed drags even when the source requested Copy, allowing an external target to negotiate a destructive operation.

proposed_comments.title: Do not advertise Move for copy-only external drags
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not advertise Move for copy-only external drags

**Severity:** `high`

The `AllowedOperations` expression unconditionally adds `Move`, while a data-backed external drag can have `RequestedOperation == Copy`. This lets an external drop target negotiate a move even though the source did not authorize one. Preserve the operation requested by external data packages, use `Move` only for shelf-only drags, and have the internal shelf targets accept the source's negotiated operation while performing the shelf action.

confidence.rationale: CommandKind.Directory is supported and the helper handles StorageFolder, but this filter deterministically excludes directories.

proposed_comments.title: Include directory bookmarks in filesystem drags
proposed_comments.body:
### Include directory bookmarks in filesystem drags

**Severity:** `medium`

The local path filter accepts file-like classifications and `File.Exists` only. `CommandKind.Directory` is supported by the classifier and the data-package helper can represent folders, but directory bookmarks therefore get no drag data package. Include directory classifications and validate them with `Directory.Exists` so folder bookmarks can be dragged as storage items.

```suggestion
        var localFilePath =
            classification.Kind is CommandKind.FileExecutable or CommandKind.FileDocument or CommandKind.Shortcut or CommandKind.InternetShortcut or CommandKind.Directory &&
            (File.Exists(classification.Target) || Directory.Exists(classification.Target))
                ? classification.Target
                : null;
```

confidence.rationale: Recent-first resolution intentionally lets the recent section own duplicate display items, so item.IsPinned cannot reliably represent whether the command remains persisted in the pin list.

proposed_comments.title: Separate persisted pin ownership from shelf-section membership
proposed_comments.body:
### Separate persisted pin ownership from shelf-section membership

**Severity:** `medium`

With recent commands shown first, a command that is both recent and persisted as pinned is displayed in the recent section, so `item.IsPinned` is false even though the settings still contain the pin. Computing `CanPin` from that section flag exposes a pin target that `TryPinItem` must reject, while the same flag is also used to decide reorder eligibility. Track persisted pin ownership separately: use it to compute `CanPin` and reorder eligibility, while keeping section membership only for remove-from-section behavior.
